iut_type: How to confirm registration completion via My Page, and the alarming-but-benign '×Withdraw Product' UI label that appears only to the Listing Owner
customer_question: What should we look at to be confident our registration has actually completed? Also, when searching for our product's DN, each product model number's right-edge column shows '×Withdraw Product' -- this display worried us. What does it mean?
question_variants: Where in My Page can a registrant verify their product's certification status?
Does a 'Withdraw Product' label next to a listed product mean it has already been withdrawn?
actual_issue: The customer wanted a reliable way to confirm their registration had actually completed, and separately became alarmed upon noticing a '×Withdraw Product' label displayed next to their product's listing when searching by DN, fearing this indicated their registration had already been cancelled or withdrawn.
plain_english_explanation: To confirm registration completion, the registrant should log into My Page, click [Manage Submitted Products] from the top menu, and check the resulting [Member Company's Qualified Products] list -- any DN/QDID appearing there has completed certification registration. Regarding the '×Withdraw Product' label: this is not an indicator that the product has already been withdrawn -- it is a UI element displayed ONLY to the Listing Owner (not visible to the general public or other companies viewing the same listing), functioning as an action button/link that initiates a deletion request for that specific Product List entry if the registrant ever wants to remove it. Clicking it proceeds to a deletion-request page, but simply seeing the label does not mean any deletion action has occurred or is pending -- the product remains fully registered and certified unless the registrant actually completes that deletion request. This deletion feature is intended for three scenarios: no longer planning to sell a registered model, sales of that model having ended, or correcting a registration mistake by removing the erroneous entry after re-registering correctly. Using it for the first two scenarios is entirely optional -- there is no obligation to remove a discontinued or never-launched model from the Product List. The only firm, mandatory obligation is the opposite one: any model name that has actually been publicly disclosed (via market sales, mail-order, a website product page, or a press release) must be registered in the Product List. The label itself carries no status meaning at all -- SIG's site mechanically displays the '×Withdraw Product' text link on the right edge of every single Product List entry, regardless of that entry's actual status; it is not a smart indicator and not a NO/YES status toggle. The reason SIG built it this confusing way (rather than simply letting the Listing Owner directly edit Product List entries) is to prevent a specific gaming scenario: if direct editing were allowed, a company notified by SIG about an unregistered product could simply rename an already-registered, unrelated model to match the flagged unregistered model name, erasing evidence that the product had ever been unregistered. The link is purely a click-to-act mechanism -- clicking it is the ONLY way anything happens; not clicking it leaves the current registration completely untouched.
consultant_answer: To confirm completion, log into My Page, click [Manage Submitted Products], and check the [Member Company's Qualified Products] list -- any DN/QDID shown there is fully registered. The '×Withdraw Product' label you saw isn't an indication that your product has been withdrawn -- it's a Listing-Owner-only UI element that lets you initiate a deletion request for that Product List entry if you ever want to remove it. Just seeing the label doesn't mean anything has happened; your product remains fully registered unless you actually click through and complete that deletion request. This feature is meant for three scenarios: (1) after Product List registration, you no longer plan to sell that model; (2) sales of that model have ended; (3) you noticed a registration mistake and, after re-registering correctly, want to remove the mistaken entry. Importantly, requesting deletion for scenarios (1) and (2) is NOT mandatory -- it's perfectly fine for a model that's no longer marketed to remain listed in the Product List indefinitely. The one firm obligation runs the other direction: any model name that HAS been publicly disclosed (through market sales, mail-order, a website product page, or a press release) MUST be registered in the Product List.
decision_logic: When a customer asks how to confirm registration completion, point them to My Page's Manage Submitted Products > Member Company's Qualified Products list; when a customer is alarmed by a '×Withdraw Product' label next to their listing, reassure them this is a Listing-Owner-only deletion-request action button, not an indicator of actual withdrawal status.
final_recommendation: Proactively explain the Manage Submitted Products verification path and the benign nature of the '×Withdraw Product' label when onboarding a customer to My Page's post-registration interface, since this label's alarming appearance (despite being harmless) is a predictable source of customer concern.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer who misunderstands the '×Withdraw Product' label as an actual withdrawal indicator might panic unnecessarily or even accidentally click through and initiate a real deletion request for a product that was never actually at risk.
